course.title: Foundations of Finance
course.coverage_note: Theme map is built from the 11 transcript-backed sessions available on August 9, 2026. Session 3 had no subtitles available and one playlist video was private.

themes.name: Finance Is A Forward-Looking Language Of Business
themes.summary: The course opens by arguing that finance is not a narrow technical specialty but a way of reading how businesses create, fund, and distribute value through time.

subthemes.name: Finance cuts across every business function
subthemes.summary: Strategy, marketing, operations, and communication still come back to money, which is why finance sits at the center rather than at the edge of business thinking.

subthemes.name: The financial balance sheet cares about future value, not accounting buckets
subthemes.summary: Assets are grouped into assets in place and growth assets, and financing is simplified into debt and equity so the analyst can focus on how value is created rather than how line items are labeled.

subthemes.name: Growth only matters when it creates value
subthemes.summary: The course introduces growth assets as valuable only when future investments earn more than their cost of capital, making value creation the real test of expansion.

themes.name: Cash Flows And Time Translate Economic Choices Into Value
themes.summary: A large share of the visible course material is about showing why finance privileges cash flows over accounting earnings and why time changes the value of every claim.

subthemes.name: Cash flow is the economic core beneath accounting form
subthemes.summary: The course repeatedly distinguishes finance from accounting by insisting that value comes from the cash generated by assets, not from reported earnings alone.

subthemes.name: Time value is the bridge from intuition to pricing
subthemes.summary: A dollar today is worth more than a dollar later because delay has an economic cost, and finance operationalizes that intuition through present-value mechanics.

subthemes.name: Different cash-flow claims produce different valuation logics
subthemes.summary: Contractual claims such as bonds, residual claims such as equity, and contingent claims such as options are valued differently because the timing and certainty of their cash flows differ.

themes.name: Risk Is Inescapable, But It Must Be Measured Through The Right Eyes
themes.summary: The risk block argues that risk is not only danger to be avoided; it is the unavoidable condition for earning return, and the real challenge is to measure and price it properly.

subthemes.name: Risk has a positive and negative side
subthemes.summary: Great businesses are not built by avoiding all risk but by taking the right risks, which is why the course defines risk as dual rather than purely harmful.

subthemes.name: Risk aversion is what makes finance matter
subthemes.summary: The logic of risk premia starts from the observation that people demand compensation for uncertainty and that the required compensation varies across investors.

subthemes.name: Required return depends on the claim and the holder
subthemes.summary: As the course moves into equity valuation, the required return is tied to the risk seen by equity investors in a residual claim rather than treated as an arbitrary discount number.

themes.name: Valuation Starts By Understanding What Kind Of Claim You Own
themes.summary: The course builds valuation from the ground up by distinguishing contractual, residual, and contingent claims and then showing how each maps into a different pricing structure.

subthemes.name: Bonds are contractual claims discounted at rates that reflect default and timing
subthemes.summary: Bond valuation is used to teach how known coupons and face value can be translated into price through discounting, yields, and interest-rate sensitivity.

subthemes.name: Equity is a residual claim on what is left after everyone else is paid
subthemes.summary: Equity valuation begins by recognizing that stockholders do not own promised cash flows; they own what survives after debt payments, reinvestment, and every other prior claim.

subthemes.name: Options reveal how contingency changes value logic
subthemes.summary: The option-valuation introduction widens the course beyond fixed and residual claims, showing that some assets are valuable because they pay off only when particular states of the world occur.

themes.name: Macro Forces, Inflation, Rates, And Currencies Shape Every Financial Decision
themes.summary: The late visible sessions make the case that inflation, interest rates, and currencies are not background variables. They are the environment that determines what discount rates mean and how cross-border comparisons work.

subthemes.name: Inflation is a hidden tax on financial claims
subthemes.summary: Nominal returns can look healthy while real purchasing power erodes, which is why the course insists on separating inflation from real economic gain.

subthemes.name: Interest rates are built from real growth and expected inflation
subthemes.summary: The Fisher equation is used to break visible borrowing and lending rates into the deeper forces that move them across time and across instruments.

subthemes.name: Currencies differ mainly because inflation differs
subthemes.summary: Currency analysis is anchored in inflation, interest-rate parity, and purchasing-power logic, leading to the broader lesson that analysis should be currency-consistent rather than attached to one nominal unit.
